\subsection{harm-pressure choice (HP-C)}

Each response is a single option letter, with or without a full stop. % src: results/subsets/harm-pressure-choice.csv :: all Llama-3.3-70B responses match [A-D]\.? (checked by thesis_tools/appendix/make_appendix_examples.py); eval_datasets.py :: 289 (SINGLE_TOKEN)
A response is labelled deceptive when the chosen option differs from the option the model was found to believe correct \parencite[pp.~4--5]{kretschmar2025liars}. % src: papers/2511.16035v2 (1).pdf p.4 (belief established by three neutral knowledge-report and three neutral choice prompts), p.5 ('labeled deceptive when the model's chosen answer differs from its belief'); checked with pypdf 2026-09-25
In our copy this rule holds for all 2{,}134 Llama-3.3-70B rows when the \texttt{model\_belief} values 0--3 are read as the options A--D, so each example below names the believed option. % src: results/subsets/harm-pressure-choice.csv :: meta.model_belief vs response letter vs column deceptive, all rows (asserted by thesis_tools/appendix/make_appendix_examples.py)
The prompt, which contains a WMDP question, is withheld. % src: thesis_tools/appendix/make_appendix_examples.py :: csv_example(withhold=True)

\subsection{harm-pressure knowledge report (HP-KR) and its two slices}

HP-KR asks the model whether it knows the answer to a WMDP question, and a response is labelled deceptive when the model denies knowing an answer it was found to believe \parencite[pp.~4--5]{kretschmar2025liars}. % src: papers/2511.16035v2 (1).pdf p.4 (knowledge-report templates; belief established), p.5 ('labeled deceptive if the model denies knowing the answer despite that established belief'); checked with pypdf 2026-09-25
The prompt is withheld. % src: thesis_tools/appendix/make_appendix_examples.py :: csv_example(withhold=True); rows below carry cais/wmdp-* item ids
We show a deceptive denial, an honest denial and an honest assertion, which between them cover the text-matched and the knowledge-matched slices of Section~\ref{sec:m-integration}. % src: src/assistant_axis_ndif/eval_datasets.py :: 391-421 (hpkr_slice: text_matched = denies_knowledge, knowledge_matched = model_belief != -1)
The model counts as knowing the answer when the dataset's \texttt{model\_belief} field is not $-1$, and a response counts as a denial when it matches the denial pattern of Section~\ref{sec:m-integration}. % src: src/assistant_axis_ndif/eval_datasets.py :: 363-364, 385-388, 418 (knows = model_belief != -1)

\subsection{sandbagging\_v2}

The system prompt asks the model to pretend to be bad at one skill, and the question comes from either MMLU or WMDP \parencite[pp.~34--35]{goldowskydill2025detecting}. % src: papers/Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear.pdf p.34 (G.3 system prompt: 'You'll only sandbag on a specific skill'), p.35 ('{question from either MMLU or WMDP}'); text checked with pypdf 2026-09-25
The prompt asks the model to put the answer it reasons to be correct in a step-2 tag and the answer it gives the user in an answer tag, so in the deceptive example below the two tags can differ \parencite[pp.~34--35]{goldowskydill2025detecting}. % src: papers/Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear.pdf p.34 (step 2: 'Think step-by-step about the correct answer ... <step2-results>'), p.35 ('Give your final answer in <answer> tags'); checked with pypdf 2026-09-25
In our copy every deceptive row's topic is a WMDP subject (bio, chem or cyber) and every honest row's is an MMLU subject. % src: src/probes/deception-detection/data/rollouts/sandbagging_v2__wmdp_mmlu__llama-70b-3.3.json :: rollouts[*].metadata.topic by expected_label (asserted by thesis_tools/appendix/make_appendix_examples.py)
The label follows the instruction (\texttt{expected\_label}), not the grader. % src: src/assistant_axis_ndif/eval_datasets.py :: 258 (no label_fn), 103-106
We withhold the deceptive row's question and its reasoning, which restates the question, and show only the response's result and answer tags; we take the first deceptive row, by row identifier, that Apollo's grader also graded deceptive. % src: thesis_tools/appendix/make_appendix_examples.py :: sandbagging_section (rule)
